fixes.explanation: Yep, the mouth, friend. David says, "I will watch my ways so that I will not sin with my tongue; I will guard my mouth with a muzzle…" (Psalm 39:1). He says the guarding is so he will not sin with his tongue. Honestly, we've all had a moment where a muzzle would've saved us a whole conversation.
Not the eyes, friend. David never mentions them here. He says he will watch his ways "…so that I will not sin with my tongue…" (Psalm 39:1). The thing he guards with a muzzle is his mouth.

You'd think all that silence would bring some calm, friend. But David says the opposite: "My heart grew hot within me; as I mused, the fire burned." (Psalm 39:3). Then he tells us, "Then I spoke with my tongue…" (Psalm 39:3). Quiet on the outside, a fire on the inside.

Friends don't appear in this part at all, baker. David says, "I have become mute; I do not open my mouth because of what You have done." (Psalm 39:9). He's talking straight to the Lord. The "You" in that line is the Lord, not his friends.

That's right, baker. David says, "For I am a foreigner dwelling with You, a stranger like all my fathers." (Psalm 39:12). He puts himself in the same line as his fathers. He calls them strangers, just like him.
